questions.question: Electric devices like laundry iron, electric toaster, electric oven, electric kettle and electric heater are based on which effect of electric current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The heating effect of electric current is utilized in devices like laundry iron, electric toaster, electric oven, electric kettle, and electric heater.
 
• When an electric current flows through a conductor, it produces heat due to the resistance to the flow of electrons in the conductor.
 
• The heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance of the conductor, and the time for which the current flows (Joule's law of heating).
 
• This principle is employed in various household appliances to generate heat for different purposes such as cooking, heating water, and ironing clothes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical effect of electric current**

 
 
• When an electric current passes through a conducting solution, it causes chemical reactions. This is known as the chemical effect of electric current.
 
• Examples include electroplating, electrolysis, and battery operation.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic effect of electric current**
 
 
• An electric current flowing through a wire creates a magnetic field around it. This is known as the magnetic effect of electric current.
 
• Applications include electric motors, generators, and transformers.
 
 
 
• **Physiological effect of electric current**
 
 
• The physiological effect refers to the impact of electric current on living tissues.
 
• Electric shocks, nerve stimulation, and muscle contractions are examples of physiological effects.

questions.question: The resistance of a 10 m long copper wire is R ohm. What will be the resistance of a 5 m long copper wire?

• The resistance **(R)** of a wire is directly proportional to its **length (L)** and inversely proportional to its **cross-sectional area (A)**.
 
• The relation is given by the formula: **R = ρ × (L / A)**, where **ρ** is the resistivity of the material.
 
• If the length of the wire is halved (from **10 m** to **5 m**), keeping the material and cross-sectional area constant, the resistance will also be halved.
 
• Hence, the resistance of the 5 m long copper wire will be **0.5R**, which is half the resistance of the 10 m long wire.
 
• This is because the resistance is directly proportional to the length of the wire, and reducing the length proportionally reduces the resistance.
 
• **Copper**, being a good conductor, has a low resistivity, ensuring minimal resistance even for longer wires.
 
• This principle is widely used in designing electrical systems, ensuring optimal wire lengths for specific applications.

questions.question: The equivalent resistance of the series combination of R ohm and 5 ohm is 7 ohm. Here, R is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **series combination**, the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula for the **equivalent resistance** in a series combination is: **Rₑq = R₁ + R₂**.
 
• Here, the equivalent resistance is given as **7 ohm**, and one of the resistances is **5 ohm**.
 
• Using the formula: **7 = R + 5**.
 
• Rearranging the equation gives: **R = 7 - 5**, which equals **2 ohm**.
 
• Hence, the missing resistance value **(R)** is **2 ohm**.
 
• This concept is fundamental in understanding **electric circuits** and is used to calculate the total resistance in a series connection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Combination**__

 __
 
• In a **series circuit**, the current flowing through each resistor is the same, but the total voltage is divided across the resistors.
 
• The total resistance in a series circuit is always greater than the resistance of any individual resistor.
 
• Series circuits are commonly used in applications like **string lights** and **simple electronic devices**.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Combination**__
 __
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the voltage across each resistor is the same, but the current is divided among the resistors.
 
• The equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is always less than the resistance of any individual resistor.
 
• Parallel circuits are widely used in **household electrical wiring** to ensure consistent voltage across all devices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistance Calculations**__
 
 
• Resistance calculations are crucial in designing **electrical circuits**, ensuring safety, and optimizing performance.
 
• They are used in industries like **electronics**, **automobiles**, and **power generation**.

questions.question: The equivalent resistance of the combination of resistors, when 1 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel, is _____.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Resistors: 1 ohm and 2 ohm connected in parallel.

**Concept Used:**

For resistors in parallel, the equivalent resistance (Rₑq) is given by:

1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ R₁ = 1 ohm, R₂ = 2 ohm

⇒ 1/Rₑq = 1/1 + 1/2

⇒ 1/Rₑq = 1 + 1/2

⇒ 1/Rₑq = (2 + 1)/2

⇒ 1/Rₑq = 3/2

⇒ Rₑq = 2/3 ohm

**∴ The equivalent resistance is 2/3 ohm.**

questions.question: For current carrying circular loop, the field strength is:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The magnetic field strength in a current-carrying circular loop is **maximum at the center** of the loop.
 
• At the center of the loop, the magnetic field lines are **most concentrated**, leading to the highest field strength.
 
• As you move towards the periphery of the loop, the magnetic field strength **decreases**.
 
• The magnetic field strength at the center of a circular loop is given by the formula **B = (μ₀I)/(2R)**, where B is the magnetic field, μ₀ is the permeability of free space, I is the current, and R is the radius of the loop.
 
• This concept is based on the **Biot-Savart law** which describes the magnetic field generated by a steady current.

• It states that the magnetic field at a point is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the current element.

• This rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.
 
• According to this rule, if you point the thumb of your right hand in the direction of the current, the direction in which your fingers curl gives the direction of the magnetic field.

questions.question: Consider a parallel combination of 2 resistors with resistances 4 Ω and 6 Ω. The equivalent resistance of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2.4Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When resistors are connected in a **parallel combination**, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula for the equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is:

 **1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂**, where R₁ and R₂ are the resistances of the individual resistors.
 
• Here, the given resistances are **4Ω** and **6Ω**.
 
• Substitute the values into the formula:

 **1/R_eq = 1/4 + 1/6**.
 
• Find the least common denominator (LCD) of 4 and 6, which is **12**. Rewrite the fractions:

 **1/R_eq = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12**.
 
• Reciprocate the result to find the equivalent resistance:

 **R_eq = 12/5 = 2.4Ω**.
 
• Thus, the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is **2.4Ω**.
 
• Parallel circuits are commonly used in **electrical systems** to ensure that the voltage across each component is the same and to reduce the overall resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

questions.question: A negatively charged glass rod attracts a hanging object. The nature of the hanging object is:

options.text: may be positively charged or may be neutral
may be negatively charged or may be neutral

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A negatively charged object will attract an object that is either positively charged or neutral due to electrostatic forces.
 
• When a charged rod is brought near a neutral object, it can induce a separation of charges within the neutral object, leading to attraction.
 
• If the hanging object is positively charged, it will naturally be attracted to the negatively charged rod due to opposite charges attracting.
 
• Neutral objects are attracted to charged objects because the induced charges within the neutral object create a net attractive force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrostatic Force**

 
 
• It is the force of attraction or repulsion between two charged objects.
 
• Like charges repel each other, whereas opposite charges attract each other.
 
 
 
• **Induced Charge**
 
 
• When a charged object is brought near a neutral object, it can cause a redistribution of charges within the neutral object.
 
• This phenomenon is known as electrostatic induction.
 
 
 
• **Conductors vs. Insulators**
 
 
• Conductors allow the free movement of electrons and can easily become charged.
 
• Insulators do not allow free movement of electrons and hold their charges tightly.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb's Law**
 
 
• This law quantifies the amount of force between two stationary, electrically charged particles.
 
• The force is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

questions.question: On which of the following scientific principles does a hydroelectric power generator work?

options.text: Conversion of gravitational potential energy into electrical energy using flowing water
Extraction of geothermal energy of ocean to produce electricity
Separation of hydrogen from water and then burning it to generate electricity
Heating water to produce steam and then running steam engine to generate electricity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conversion of gravitational potential energy into electrical energy using flowing water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hydroelectric power plants** convert the **gravitational potential energy** of water stored at a height into electrical energy.
 
• The process involves water flowing from a high elevation through turbines, which then drive generators to produce electricity.
 
• The **turbines** and **generators** are the critical components in this conversion process, making use of the kinetic energy of flowing water.
 
• Hydroelectric power is a major source of renewable energy, contributing significantly to the global energy mix.
 
• Examples include large-scale facilities like the Hoover Dam in the USA and the Three Gorges Dam in China, which are among the largest hydroelectric power plants in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potential Energy:** The energy possessed by an object due to its position relative to other objects, stresses within itself, its electric charge, or other factors.
 
• **Kinetic Energy:** The energy possessed by an object due to its motion. In the context of hydroelectric power, it refers to the energy of flowing water.
 
• **Renewable Energy:** Energy from sources that are naturally replenishing but flow-limited, such as wind, solar, and hydro power.
 
• **Turbine:** A machine for producing continuous power that is typically powered by water, steam, gas, or air. In hydroelectric plants, water turbines convert water flow into mechanical energy.

questions.question: The sum of all potential changes in a closed circuit is zero. This is called _____________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kirchhoff's second rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kirchhoff's second rule**, also known as the **Voltage Law (KVL)**, states that the **algebraic sum of all potential differences (voltages)** around any closed loop in a circuit is **zero**.
 
• This rule is based on the law of conservation of energy, which implies that the total energy gained and lost by charges in a closed circuit must balance.
 
• The equation derived from this rule is: **ΣV = 0**, where V represents the voltage.
 
• The potential changes include contributions from **resistors, batteries, and other elements** in the circuit.
 
• This rule is widely applied in circuit analysis to calculate **unknown voltages and currents** in complex circuits.
 
• **Gustav Kirchhoff**, a German physicist, formulated this rule in **1845**.
 
• It complements Kirchhoff’s first rule (current law) to provide a complete framework for analyzing electrical circuits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kirchhoff's fourth rule**__

 __
 
• There is no **fourth rule** in Kirchhoff's laws. Kirchhoff's contributions are limited to the **current law (first rule)** and the **voltage law (second rule)**.
 
• Any mention of a fourth rule is likely a misinterpretation or fictional addition.
 
 
 
• **Kirchhoff's first rule**__
 __
 
• Kirchhoff's first rule is the **Current Law (KCL)**, which states that the **sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum of currents leaving the junction**.
 
• This is based on the **conservation of electric charge**.
 
 
 
• **Kirchhoff's third rule**__
 
 
• Similar to the "fourth rule," there is no separate **third rule** attributed to Kirchhoff.
 
• The **first and second rules** are the only fundamental laws established by him for circuit analysis.

questions.question: In a series combination of resistors, how is the voltage distributed across each resistor?

• The **thumb** indicates the direction of the **motion of the conductor**.
 
• The **forefinger** points in the direction of the **magnetic field**.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect the electric power consumed by an electric device?

The correct answer is __**Frequency of the device**__.

• The electric power consumed by an electric device is primarily determined by its resistance, the voltage applied to it, and the current flowing through it.
 
• Power consumption is calculated using the formula P = V x I, where P is power, V is voltage, and I is current.
 
• Ohm’s Law states that V = I x R, where R is resistance, thus power can also be expressed as P = I² x R or P = V² / R.
 
• The frequency of the device does not affect the power consumed in a DC circuit and only has an impact in AC circuits under specific conditions such as reactance in inductive or capacitive elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance (R)**

 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of current in an electrical circuit.
 
• The unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω).
 
• Higher resistance in a device leads to lower current for a given voltage, thus affecting the power consumed.
 
 
 
• **Voltage (V)**
 
 
• Voltage is the electrical potential difference between two points in a circuit.
 
• The unit of voltage is the volt (V).
 
• Increasing the voltage applied to a device increases the current and hence the power consumed, assuming resistance stays constant.
 
 
 
• **Current (I)**
 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• The unit of current is the ampere (A).
 
• For a constant voltage, increasing the resistance reduces the current, thereby decreasing power consumption.
 
 
 
• **Frequency (Hz)**
 
 
• Frequency is the number of cycles per second in an alternating current (AC) circuit.
 
• The unit of frequency is hertz (Hz).
 
• Frequency affects the reactance in AC circuits but does not directly impact power consumption in simple resistive loads.

questions.question: The number of 176-Ω resistors (in parallel) required to carry 5 A on a 220-V line is:

• **Current supplied by each resistor** = 220 / 176 = 1.25 A; total current = 1.25 × 4 = 5 A.

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of most conductors as their temperature increases?

__
 
• As the temperature of most **conductors** increases, their **resistance** also increases.
 
• This happens because atoms in the conductor vibrate more at higher temperatures, causing more frequent collisions with electrons.
 
• These collisions impede the flow of electrons, which leads to an increase in resistance.
 
• The relationship between temperature and resistance in conductors is generally **linear** over a moderate range of temperatures.
 
• This behavior can be described by the **temperature coefficient of resistance**, which is positive for most conductors.
 
• Materials like **copper, aluminum, and silver** exhibit this increase in resistance with temperature.
 
• This principle is crucial in designing electrical and electronic components, as it affects the performance and efficiency of these devices.

__

 __
 
• This statement is true only for **superconductors**, which are special materials that exhibit zero resistance below a certain critical temperature.
 
• Superconductivity is a quantum mechanical phenomenon and is not exhibited by ordinary conductors like copper or aluminum.
 
 
 
• **It decreases.**__
 __
 
• This behavior is characteristic of **semiconductors** and **insulators** rather than conductors.
 
• In semiconductors, an increase in temperature provides energy to electrons, allowing them to jump into the conduction band, thus decreasing resistance.
 
 
 
• **It remains the same.**__
 
 
• This is generally not true for conductors as their resistance changes with temperature.
 
• However, some **special materials** and **alloys** are designed to have a very low temperature coefficient of resistance, making their resistance relatively stable over a range of temperatures.

• **Electric Current:**

• **Coulomb (C):**

• It is defined as the amount of charge transported by a constant current of one Ampere in one second.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Electric Current:**
 
 
• The formula to calculate electric current is I = Q / t, where I is the current, Q is the charge, and t is the time.

questions.question: Which of the following is equal to 1 Ohm (If V and A are volt and ampere, respectively)?

The Correct answer is __**1V/1A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Ohm** is the unit of **electrical resistance** in the **International System of Units (SI)**.
 
• It is named after **Georg Simon Ohm**, a German physicist who formulated Ohm's law.
 
• **Ohm's Law** states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as **V = IR**, where **V** is the voltage, **I** is the current, and **R** is the resistance.
 
• Hence, **1 Ohm** is defined as the resistance that allows a current of **1 Ampere (A)** to flow when a voltage of **1 Volt (V)** is applied.
 
• This can be represented as **1 Ohm = 1V/1A**.
